atlas/payments at commit 8f31c2a, before we merge pull request 42. Customers
occasionally receive duplicate receipts when the provider times out after accepting
a charge. The patch introduces an idempotency key derived from the checkout ID

charges, and whether the new timeout handling preserves the original error.

recommended correction. Do not deploy anything. If the design looks sound, say
which failure cases you checked and what remains uncertain.

argv: Atlas payments PR 42 at 8f31c2a has a blocking worker race: persist one idempotency key per checkout transaction. Expired provider keys require reconciliation. Timeout errors are preserved. Author will correct persistence and expiry handling; no deployment or sandbox verification.
records.stdin:
I reviewed atlas/payments at commit 8f31c2a and the attached synthetic retry
trace for pull request 42. There is one blocking issue in src/checkout.rs around
the retry loop: the key is allocated inside each worker rather than persisted
with the checkout, so two workers can race and create different keys. Move key
creation into the checkout transaction and enforce a unique checkout ID in the
key table. The timeout branch preserves the original provider error correctly.
The provider expires keys after twenty four hours, so retries beyond that window
need reconciliation rather than another charge attempt. I checked the timeout
after acceptance, a successful retry, and two simultaneous workers against the
trace. I have not exercised a real provider sandbox or a database migration.
Please make the transaction change and add the reconciliation guard, then send
the new commit and the relevant existing test results. No deployment is needed
for this review; keep the change limited to checkout persistence.

worker case. Please review the transaction boundary and confirm that a rollback
cannot leave a worker using an uncommitted key. The migration has not been
deployed, and no live provider requests were made.

boundary in pull request 42. The key is returned only after commit succeeds;
the rollback path returns the database error before any provider call. Both
workers therefore converge on the stored key. The reconciliation guard also
prevents a fresh charge once the provider retention window has elapsed. One
remaining operational detail is the migration order: install the unique index
before starting workers that depend on it. Please include that order and the
rollback procedure in the release note. This is documentation follow up rather
than another code blocker. Production deployment still needs the normal human
release decision.

argv: Atlas payments PR 42 at 8f31c2a has a blocking worker race: persist one idempotency key per checkout transaction. Expired provider keys require reconciliation. Timeout errors are preserved. Author will correct persistence and expiry handling; no deployment or sandbox verification.
records.stdin:
I reviewed atlas/payments at commit 8f31c2a and the attached synthetic retry
trace for pull request 42. There is one blocking issue in src/checkout.rs around
the retry loop: the key is allocated inside each worker rather than persisted
with the checkout, so two workers can race and create different keys. Move key
creation into the checkout transaction and enforce a unique checkout ID in the
key table. The timeout branch preserves the original provider error correctly.
The provider expires keys after twenty four hours, so retries beyond that window
need reconciliation rather than another charge attempt. I checked the timeout
after acceptance, a successful retry, and two simultaneous workers against the
trace. I have not exercised a real provider sandbox or a database migration.
Please make the transaction change and add the reconciliation guard, then send
the new commit and the relevant existing test results. No deployment is needed
for this review; keep the change limited to checkout persistence.
